messages:
Michael H: Draft PRD for Dedicated capacity launch — need to lock SLA targets, throughput sizing, and autoscale acceptance criteria. Quick sync here.
Rita S: thanks — can we make the SLA concrete? p50/p95/P99 targets, per-model and per-route expectations.
Deepak P: suggested baseline from perf lab for 8k seq: p50 < 70ms, p95 < 250ms, p99 < 600ms (single-request, warmed KV). throughput per-GPU depends on model; prelim numbers: 900–2.4k tok/s for Llama variants on A100.
Quan L: cold-cache is the killer. We should call out cold vs warmed SLA and fallback behavior (queueing vs reject).
Michael H: agree. proposal: two-tier SLA — warmed (common prefixes cached): p95 < 250ms; cold: p95 < 1.2s. Availability: 99.95% monthly for Dedicated tenant endpoints.
Jen K: for launch acceptance, canary must show <0.5% errors, avg latency delta vs lab < +15%, and no tail regressions in p99 beyond +200ms.
Rita S: edge cases we need in PRD:
- steady high QPS bursts (10x baseline) for 1–5m
- massive KV invalidation events (cache thrash)
- model swap during active sessions
- degraded network to storage/KMS
Quan L: add noisy neighbor isolation tests (run synthetic noisy tenant that loads all GPUs) and confirm autoscaler prevents tenant bleed.
Deepak P: autoscale policy draft (for discussion):
```
{
  "scale_metric": "inflight_requests_per_gpu",
  "scale_up_threshold": 200,
  "scale_down_threshold": 80,
  "min_replicas": 2,
  "max_replicas": 25,
  "stabilization_window": 30,
  "grace_period": 60
}
```
Rita S: looks OK but we should use token-rate + queue-depth hybrid. inflight isn't enough for long sequences.
Michael H: acceptance criteria (short):
1) SLA verification: benched p95/p99 in prod canary within targets for warmed traffic
2) Throughput sizing validated: per-GPU throughput measured with representative prompts and meets cost model
3) Autoscale safety: no cascading scale-up that trips quotas; scale actions limited to +50% per 60s
4) Fallback policy: when capacity exhausted, requests are routed to compatible lower-cost variant with documented quality delta
5) Observability: dashboards for token-rate, inflight, cache-hit, scale-events, and alerting for tail-latency > threshold
Rita S: add test plan: small canary (5%) for 24h, monitor error rate, tail latency, cost delta. If metrics pass for 6 rolling hours, expand to 25% then full.
Quan L: what's the rollback plan? keep a manual kill switch and automated fallback to hosted model for 10% traffic during incidents.
Michael H: noted. Owner: @Rita S owns PRD edits, @Deepak P owns perf validation, @Quan L owns SRE-runbooks, @Jen K owns rollout gating.
deploy-bot: canary deployment started for tenant-redwood-dedicated v1.0 — id=deploy-9843 :rocket:
Rita S: quick question — do we need explicit per-route SLAs in PRD or leave as per-tenant defaults? some customers want route-level guarantees.
Michael H: include per-route optional SLAs (opt-in) but require higher commitment (dedicated pool sizing + extra cost).
Deepak P: one more edge case: multi-model co-hosting on same GPU. need strict packing rules to avoid KV eviction.
Rita S: I'll add packing constraints and an explicit test harness for cache thrash.
Michael H: great. next steps: Rita S to update PRD draft with the two-tier SLA + autoscale policy + test plan by EOD tomorrow. Deepak P to run a small perf matrix and post numbers in this thread. Quan L to write canary playbook.
Jen K: I'll prep the rollout checklist and infra quotas doc.
Michael H: thanks all. tagging backlog: #PRD-382 allocate docs and checklist. :white_check_mark:
Deepak P: starting perf runs now, will post results as soon as first pass completes.
Rita S: updated PRD draft uploaded to Google Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/PRD-dedicated-capacity (comment if anything missing)
Michael H: review scheduled in product sync tomorrow 10:00am PT. Please read PRD before.
Quan L: adding SLO burn alert thresholds to the canary playbook (will push in 30m).
deploy-bot: canary health check: 1m check — token-rate stable, error-rate 0.12%, p95 latency +8% vs baseline.
